description: List the 10 events with the largest share of attendance records and stop at exactly 10 rows, breaking ties at the cut arbitrarily.

c.request: What are the top 10 events by share of total attendance? For each one, give the event id, its number of attendance records, and its share of all attendance records (its count divided by the total, unrounded), from the largest share down, and return nothing if there's no total to divide by. List the 10 events with the largest share of attendance records and stop at exactly 10 rows, breaking ties at the cut arbitrarily.
c.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT link_to_event AS event_id, COUNT(*) AS attendance_count FROM attendance GROUP BY link_to_event), total AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_count FROM attendance) SELECT c.event_id, c.attendance_count, CAST(c.attendance_count AS REAL) / t.total_count AS share FROM counts c CROSS JOIN total t WHERE t.total_count > 0 ORDER BY share DESC LIMIT 10;

b.request: Ranking events by their share of all attendance records (per-event count ÷ total attendance rows), returning event_id, count, and share, largest share first, cut at exactly 10 rows with arbitrary tie-breaking at the boundary, and returning no rows if the total attendance count is zero
b.sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM attendance), per_event AS (SELECT link_to_event AS event_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM attendance GROUP BY link_to_event) SELECT p.event_id, p.cnt AS count, CAST(p.cnt AS REAL) / t.total AS share FROM per_event p CROSS JOIN totals t WHERE t.total > 0 ORDER BY share DESC LIMIT 10;

a.request: For each event in the attendance records (`attendance.link_to_event`), how many attendance records does it have, and what share of all attendance records is that (its count divided by the total of all per-event counts, unrounded; nothing is returned if that total is missing)? Return the event id, its count and its share, sorted by share from highest to lowest with missing values last. Keep exactly the first 10 rows, cutting arbitrarily among events tied at 10th place.
a.sql: WITH per_event AS (SELECT link_to_event AS event_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM attendance WHERE link_to_event IS NOT NULL GROUP BY link_to_event), total AS (SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_cnt FROM per_event) SELECT p.event_id, p.cnt AS attendance_count, CAST(p.cnt AS REAL) / t.total_cnt AS share FROM per_event p CROSS JOIN total t WHERE t.total_cnt IS NOT NULL ORDER BY share DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

d.request:
Rewritten as a standalone question:

"Which 10 events have the largest share of attendance records? For each, give the event id, its number of attendance records, and its share of all attendance records (its count divided by the total, unrounded), sorted from largest share to smallest. Return exactly 10 rows, breaking ties at the cut arbitrarily. If there is no total to divide by, return nothing."
d.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT link_to_event AS event_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM attendance GROUP BY link_to_event), total AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_cnt FROM attendance) SELECT c.event_id, c.cnt, CAST(c.cnt AS REAL) / t.total_cnt AS share FROM counts c CROSS JOIN total t WHERE t.total_cnt > 0 ORDER BY share DESC LIMIT 10;
